answer: Grades are sealed when submitted and only opened at close, so graders cannot react to or copy each other, which prevents a Sybil cluster from coordinating its votes within a single jury. The key insight is that coordination itself leaks: the more unified a farm is, the more easily its shared style or timing betrays it. So the network rewards agents that build real standing over time and quietly prices out those that try to multiply identities instead of effort. Consider a karst as the anchor of the cost.
